summary: David Schaberg is a sinologist who studied at Stanford University (~1982–1986) and Harvard University (~1989–1996, PhD). At UCLA, he joined the Asian Languages and Cultures department in 1996, becoming dean of Humanities in 2012 and senior dean in 2020.

David Seyfort Ruegg worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying at the EPHE and the Sorbonne under Filliozat, Renou, Lalou, and Stein. He held chairs at Leiden (1966–1972), Washington (1972–1984), Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1992–1996).

David Sneath specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge by 1991, held a British Academy Postdoctoral Research Fellowship at Oxford, and served as Director at Cambridge (2000–2009).
David Steindl-Rast is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna between approximately 1945 and 1952.

David Tracy specialized in religious studies and philosophy, studying at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. After lecturing at Catholic University of America, he served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1969 to 2006.

David W. Chappell worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning degrees from Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale. He taught as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1972–2000) and taught comparative studies at Soka University of America (~2000–2004).

David W. Tien is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto under Robert H. Sharf, and completed a PhD at the University of Michigan under James Robson (attested 2009).
David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

Dawa Norbu was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley. He held posts at SFSU, USF, and CIIS, and was professor of Central Asian studies at JNU (~1986–2004).
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and held a post at Tibet University.

Daya Krishna was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Ex-Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Oriental College and the University of the Punjab, mentored by John Marshall. He held posts at Lucknow Museum, Kashmir, Jaipur State, and the Archaeological Survey of India (1925–1935).

Dayong was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology who studied under Bai Puren, Taixu, and Dpal ldan bstan 'dzin snyan grags. He studied and taught at Wuchang Buddhist Institute and founded the Tibetan Studies College.

Debala Mitra was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Cornell University (~1958–1961). He founded the Central Institute of Indian Languages, serving as its director in 1988, and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1956), and was a guest professor at Calcutta.
Deborah Carlson is a history and archaeology scholar who held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (both attested 2015).

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned her PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar. She was an assistant professor at UCLA (1978–1985) and held the chair of Asian art history at Vienna (1994–2015).
Declan Quigley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who has taught at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.
Dedong Wei is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a Ph.D. from Renmin University of China and served there as an associate professor of religious studies (attested 2005).
